analysis.title: Cheatsheet - US Midterms: A final markets guide
key_insights: Citi's base case is divided government, with a toss-up on whether Democrats flip only the House or also retake the Senate. Kalshi puts a Democratic sweep at 63% and a Democratic House with a Republican Senate at 27%. Nate Silver sees a 75% chance of a Democratic Senate win.

The House is broadly expected to flip because Democrats need only five seats. Cook rates 220 seats as favoring Democrats versus 198 for Republicans, and toss-ups have narrowed to 17 from 22 a month ago. A slim Democratic majority would limit legislative ability and raise gridlock risk.

The Senate matters more for markets. Summer polling strength has lost momentum, with razor-thin margins in Iowa, Kansas, Alaska and Maine. Eleven states are competitive and Texas is the key bellwether. Redistricting and the map give Republicans a structural edge.

Historically the president's party loses an average of 26 House seats in midterms since 1946 and about four Senate seats. Trump's second-term net approval is -21.6 versus -11.6 for Biden and -7.8 for Trump's first term at the same point. Democrats lead the generic ballot by 9.1.

Early voting: 40m+ ballots cast as of Oct 28, with registered Democrats at 44.3% of early votes in states reporting party registration versus 31.2% for Republicans. About 46m early ballots were cast in 2022.

Election night timeline: the earliest House clues come 19:30-20:00 ET (Kentucky, Ohio, Florida). North Carolina and Texas results from 21:00 ET. Citi expects NC, NH, GA, KS, OH and TX Senate results potentially on the night, from about 22:00 ET. MA, MI and MN may wait until the next day. California House races and Alaska's Senate race may stay unresolved past election night.

Midterms are a secondary market focus behind macro. A Democratic sweep is increasingly priced in. Citi sees the Senate as a genuine toss-up, and a sweep by either party would produce a larger market move than a split outcome.

Citi Global Macro Strategy finds that day-one price action after midterms has negative follow-through in the following days. A pullback after a Democratic sweep would be a buy-the-dip opportunity for SPX and DXY. USTs generally show flat or positive t+1 action with the curve flattening.

Event jump risk is priced at +/-0.93% for SPX. GBPUSD carries the largest vol premium among G10 majors at about 3.5 vol points. Credit, rates and equities tend to underperform in election years, with a post-election relief rally unwinding that volatility into year-end.

Positioning: investors are adding bearish US equity positions, USD remains net long with outflow risk after last week's leveraged selling, and treasuries recently flipped tactically long but remain structurally short. Treasury refunding on Nov 4 should draw more focus.

Geopolitics: reports say the Trump administration is evaluating military action in the Middle East after the midterms. Escalation with Iran would likely lift oil and USD and weigh on risk assets. Russia-Ukraine remains an uncertainty for European growth, energy and defense spending.

Fiscal: Citi economists expect no meaningful change to the fiscal outlook even with a Democratic sweep, though a sweep implies slightly looser policy, such as delaying scheduled Medicare cuts ($1tn over 10 years) and SNAP cuts (~$120bn). Citi D1's favored basket is Healthcare Levered to AI (CGUSHCAI Index).

A budget or continuing resolution is needed during the lame duck period to avoid a shutdown on December 11. Treasury can issue an additional $1.2tn under the soft debt ceiling, with a potential X-date in Q4 2027. Negotiations are expected to go down to the wire.

Trade policy should stay unchanged. Citi expects the US effective tariff rate to hold near current levels (Yale Budget Lab: 11.0%). USMCA annual reviews leave uncertainty for Mexico and Canada, and China's tariff truce expires January 10, 2027.
AI regulation should stay at state level until the 2028 elections. The election is unlikely to alter the AI investment cycle but could affect how it is regulated.
Impeachment risk may fall on cabinet officials rather than Trump. A Senate conviction needs a two-thirds majority and is unlikely. Citi expects more noise but limited market impact.

tension_points.bull_case: Democrats could win the Senate, as Nate Silver gives a 75% chance and Kalshi puts a Democratic sweep at 63%. A Texas win would signal a broader blue wave.
tension_points.bear_case: Citi sees the Senate as a genuine toss-up. Democratic summer polling has lost momentum, margins are razor-thin in Iowa, Kansas, Alaska and Maine, and redistricting and the map favor Republicans.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Democratic loss in Texas, the key bellwether, would undercut the blue-wave case. Early signals are Kentucky and Ohio gains and Florida holds from 19:30-20:00 ET.

theme_stances.key_argument: Midterms remain a secondary focus behind macro, and a sweep by either party would produce a larger market move than a split outcome.
